doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His father's college and his father's character
summary: Livingstone College, an educator family, and a not very strict preacher father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I’d like to return to what we started off with yesterday, and speak a bit more about your family. You had some information you were going to think of. For one thing, I’m not sure whether we got on tape what college your father went to.
He was a minister. Was that a theological college? A seminary?
No... I don’t know. It might have been. But he was one of the first black students there. It was the oldest black college. I don’t know exactly what they taught there.
You said your whole family were educators.
Me, too. I’m the most educated. No, what I was saying was most of them had doctorates. I got a Bachelors, but they got...
Oh, educators. Oh, yeah. All of them were educators, right. All of them went into education. Schoolteachers and people like that.
Can you talk about what kind of person your father was? Was he very strict.

Ah, he was... It’s hard for me to say. He was just a father. He wasn’t that strict because I never did anything to make him angry. He was a preacher and an insurance salesman, and every Sunday I had my duties and the regular stuff I had to do. But other than that, he was ok. Heh-heh.
